quickAnswer: Enterprise and corporate campus cleaning across buildings 25,000 sq ft and larger averages $0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft per visit ($0.07–$0.12/sq ft for 10,000–24,999 sq ft regional hubs), plus $15 to $30 per restroom. On a 5x/week schedule (21.65 visits/month), a 50,000 sq ft mixed-floor headquarters with 12 restrooms runs $55,045 to $110,090 per month ($2,542–$5,085/visit), while a 100,000 sq ft campus with 20 restrooms averages $108,791 to $217,582 per month.

blocks.text: Procurement at **25,000 to 500,000+ sq ft** operates on entirely different mechanics than single-suite janitorial contracts. At corporate headquarters, R&D parks, and multi-building campuses, drive-time mobilization disappears because dedicated crews stage ride-on scrubbers, wide-area carpet extractors, and bulk chemical dispensers inside permanent on-site closets. That scale compresses base US cleaning rates into the **$0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft per visit** bracket (compared with **$0.07 to $0.12/sq ft** in 10,000–24,999 sq ft branch offices).

Yet lower unit rates still generate six- and seven-figure annual facilities spend, where a **$0.01/sq ft estimating error** or sloppy cleanable-footage measurement costs **$50,000+ per year**. Before issuing an enterprise RFP, anchor your internal baseline with our [Office Cleaning Cost Guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) benchmarks and compare [medium office janitorial pricing](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/medium-office-janitorial-pricing-models/) for smaller regional satellites.
Enterprise & Corporate Campus Cost Benchmarks (15,000–150,000 Sq Ft)

Large corporate buildings almost universally run **5x/week weekday service (`21.65` visits/month at a `0.90x` frequency multiplier)** or **7x/week campus schedules (`30.33` visits/month at `0.87x`)** when hosting continuous operations, cafeterias, or weekend security desks. blocks.text: Day Porters, Shift Specialization, and Labor-Hour Allocation

Above 25,000 sq ft, vendors stop dispatching generalist cleaners and split labor into **specialized task teams** (trash and liner pullers, restroom sanitization specialists, vacuum crews, and auto-scrubber operators) working concurrently. A **150,000 sq ft campus** requiring **42.00 to 61.07 productive labor hours per night** translates into a 7-to-10-person evening crew overseen by an on-site working lead or area supervisor.

Most campuses also layer **daytime porters** billed at **$35 to $65 per hour** (or bundled as dedicated full-time equivalents) to refresh lobby glass, empty high-traffic atrium receptacles, wipe cafeteria tables, and inspect [commercial restrooms](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-per-restroom-in-commercial-cleaning-quotes/) every two hours. Heavy specialty projects—such as post-tenant-buildout HEPA vacuuming, stone crystallization, or multi-story interior glass work—bill separately at **$55 to $95 per specialty hour**.
Cleanable vs. BOMA Rentable Footage and Union Cost Multipliers

The single fastest way to overpay on a 50,000+ sq ft building is pricing off **BOMA gross rentable square footage** instead of **net cleanable square footage**. Mechanical rooms, electrical closets, stairwell shafts, IDF data rooms, loading docks, and unoccupied shell floors often represent **10% to 18%** of gross building area. Removing non-cleanable zones from a 100,000 sq ft RFP saves **$11,000 to $35,000 per month** immediately.

blocks.title: Enterprise COI, E-Verify, Union Wage, and OSHA Documentation
blocks.text: Corporate campuses typically require $1M/$2M Commercial General Liability paired with a $5M umbrella policy, statutory Workers' Compensation, janitorial fidelity bonding, E-Verify and background checks for badged night access, OSHA HazCom (29 CFR 1910.1200) SDS stations on every floor, and Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) compliance for campus fitness centers and medical rooms. In union downtown markets (such as Manhattan, Chicago, or San Francisco), local prevailing wage and benefit packages push total rates 1.25x to 1.35x above the US baseline.
Amortized Floor Care, Consumables, and High-Throughput Campus Tooling

Enterprise facilities almost always separate nightly maintenance from **amortized quarterly deep floor care ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/month)**—which equates to **$1,500 to $3,000/month** on a 50,000 sq ft campus for scheduled encapsulation carpet care, auto-scrubbing, and VCT recoat cycles. Similarly, bundling **paper, soap, and liner consumables ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit)** adds **$13,000 to $27,000/month** on a 50,000 sq ft 5x/week building, making competitive direct-ship jan-san distribution contracts worth auditing alongside labor.

To keep [janitorial production rates](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/how-janitorial-production-rates-determine-price/) high across expansive lobbies, pantries, and glass conference wings, campus carts standardize on durable, replaceable commercial hand tools:

items: **Ettore Master Brass 14-Inch Commercial Window Squeegee:** Solid tempered brass 14-in channel with replaceable pro rubber blade designed for rapid, streak-free passes across atrium sidelights and glass conference partitions.

**O-Cedar Commercial MaxiClean Angle Broom & Lobby Pan:** 12-in flagged poly bristle broom on a 48-in handle sized for catching gritty debris along lobby baseboards, revolving door tracks, and freight elevator sills.

**3M Scotch-Brite Commercial Heavy-Duty Scour Pads (20-Pack):** Commercial 6x9 in non-rusting synthetic scouring pads engineered for campus breakroom stainless sinks, espresso stations, and cafeteria prep counters.

Enterprise RFP Governance and Monthly KPI Audit Steps

items.name: Measure Net Cleanable Sq Ft Floor by Floor
items.text: Exclude IDF closets, chiller rooms, dark shell space, and landlord-cleaned exterior plazas before issuing bid sheets.

items.name: Require Staffing Plans Showing Productive Hours and Supervision
items.text: Cross-check bidder headcount against ISSA pace (roughly 28 to 41 productive hrs/night per 100,000 sq ft) plus dedicated lead-supervisor QA hours.

items.name: Separate Labor, Consumables, and Periodic Floor Restoration
items.text: Score base janitorial labor independently from paper/soap markups ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit) and amortized carpet/VCT projects ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo).

items.name: Tie APPA Inspection Scores to Monthly Retainage or Credits
items.text: Mandate weekly joint walkthroughs using APPA Level 2 (Ordinary Tidiness) standards, digital badged timeclocks, and documented SLA corrective credits.

faqs.q: What is the average cost per square foot to clean a 50,000+ sq ft corporate campus?
faqs.a: US facilities 25,000 sq ft and larger average $0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft per visit for core nightly cleaning plus $15 to $30 per restroom. On a 5x/week schedule (21.65 visits/month), a 50,000 sq ft mixed-floor building with 12 restrooms runs $55,045 to $110,090 per month before optional consumables or day-porter coverage.

faqs.q: How is office cleaning cost per employee headcount evaluated alongside square footage?
faqs.a: Facility teams often cross-check per-sq-ft bids against active daily occupancy—covered in detail in our cost per employee headcount guide—because dense campuses (125–150 sq ft per seated worker) generate far more restroom traffic and breakroom trash than hybrid offices running at 300+ sq ft per person.

faqs.q: Do Green Seal GS-37 and LEED EBOM standards increase campus cleaning budgets?
faqs.a: Transitioning a large campus to Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice dilution concentrates typically adds 0% to 4% to chemical costs—and often lowers chemical spend through automated wall dispensers. The main LEED EBOM investment is requiring 4-level HEPA vacuums and color-coded launderable microfiber.

faqs.q: Why should enterprise RFPs exclude non-cleanable mechanical and server rooms?
faqs.a: Gross BOMA lease square footage routinely includes 10% to 18% restricted mechanical shafts, MDF/IDF server rooms, and freight lobbies. Leaving those uncleaned zones inside bid templates inflates annual contract pricing by tens of thousands of dollars for square footage crews never enter.

faqs.q: What happens if an enterprise bidder quotes below $0.04 per sq ft?
faqs.a: Sub-$0.04/sq ft bids in major US metros almost always indicate understaffed shifts, skipped periodic dusting/floor care, or off-the-books subcontracting that violates W-2 payroll, E-Verify, and Workers' Compensation requirements—creating severe security and premises liability exposure.
